title: Critical ICU Ventilator Allocation
real_world_story: An Intensive Care Unit (ICU) has M operational mechanical ventilators available. There are N patients currently suffering from acute hypoxemic respiratory distress. Clinical evaluation assigns each patient i an oxygen saturation deficit score d_i (representing how far their blood oxygen levels have plummeted below normal). Each ventilator can support exactly 1 patient. The clinical protocol dictates allocating ventilators to the patients with the highest deficit scores first. If M >= N, every patient receives a ventilator. Determine the maximum sum of deficit scores addressed by assigning the M ventilators.
problem_statement: Given N patient deficit scores and M available ventilators, select at most min(N, M) patients such that the sum of their deficit scores is maximized.
task: Compute the sum of oxygen deficit scores addressed for the selected patients.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and M, the number of patients and the number of available ventilators.
The second line contains N space-separated integers d_1, d_2, ..., d_N, the deficit scores of the patients.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum total deficit score addressed.

examples.explanation: Sorting deficit scores in descending order gives [42, 35, 28, 15, 8]. Allocating the 3 ventilators to the top 3 patients yields 42 + 35 + 28 = 105.
There are 5 ventilators and only 3 patients. All 3 patients receive a ventilator, addressing a total deficit of 30 + 20 + 10 = 60.

real_world_takeaway: Greedy priority selection ensures that life-saving ICU machinery is assigned to the patients at greatest acute risk, maximizing overall survival benefit.
